title: Blue Team / SOC
blurb: Hunt the breach you caused. You exfiltrated a customer table in the AI Security area — now work the same incident from the other side: triage it, write the detection that would have caught it, and prove the control closed it.
long_description: Most SOC training hands you someone else's logs and asks you to find someone else's attack. This one hands you your own. You run the cross-tool exfiltration from the AI & Agent Security area, then work the evidence it leaves in the lab event log and the mail sink: what was taken, when, by which path, and what field would have caught it earliest. It runs on the same Docker stack as the AI area — no new services, no second environment to stand up.

env.notes: Reuses the AI Security stack unchanged. Nothing new to install; the evidence surfaces are the lab event log and the MailHog sink.

prerequisites: Finish at least scenarios 01 and 03 of AI & Agent Security
Comfortable reading JSON and a timestamped event log
outcomes: Triage an exfiltration incident from raw evidence: what, when, where, how much
Distinguish the events that describe the attack from the events that merely describe the configuration
Write a detection that keys on the harmful pattern rather than on a common one
Explain why alerting on every outbound email is a broken rule
Prove a control closed the gap, and state honestly what your evidence does not prove

credential.title: Agent Incident Triage
credential.description: Proves you can work an agent-driven exfiltration end to end: triage the evidence, write the detection, and measure the control.
